prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study was a prospective investigation into the relationship between specific cognitive deficits and white matter changes in individuals with tumors in the right side of the brain.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Thirty-four patients underwent brain imaging and four cognitive tests before surgery, while twenty-two of them were re-tested after the operation.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The control group consisted of thirty-four participants from the Human Connectome Project.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Before surgery, difficulties with spatial awareness, recognizing facial emotions, and understanding others' mental states were linked to structural abnormalities in the white matter of the right hemisphere.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Specifically, visuospatial problems were associated with changes in the frontal aslant tract, arcuate fasciculus, and two parts of the superior longitudinal fasciculus.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Deficits in recognizing facial emotions were associated with the third part of the superior longitudinal fasciculus and the uncinate fasciculus, while mentalizing deficits were linked to the arcuate fasciculus.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: After surgery, exploratory results suggested that new social-emotional deficits were associated with structural changes in the inferior longitudinal fasciculus and parts of the superior longitudinal fasciculus.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: New visuospatial deficits after surgery showed a trend toward a decrease in the volume of the right frontal aslant tract.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Compared to the control group, changes in the left hemisphere were seen in all patients, while changes in the right hemisphere were mainly found in those who had cognitive deficits.
facts.subject: humans
